settings.label: Server URL
settings.meaning: FusionAuth's base URL, such as https://auth.example.com. Its APIs, OAuth endpoints and keys (/.well-known/jwks.json) are under it.
settings.whereToFind: The address your FusionAuth instance is served at (FusionAuth Cloud: the deployment's URL). Test is another instance or tenant, with its own keys.

settings.label: API key
settings.meaning: Authenticates the backend to the User, Login, Registration, Passwordless and JWT APIs. Give it only those endpoints.
settings.whereToFind: Settings › API Keys › Add: limit it to /api/user, /api/user/registration, /api/login, /api/passwordless, /api/user/verify-email, /api/user/forgot-password, /api/user/change-password and /api/jwt/refresh.

settings.label: Application ID
settings.meaning: The application users sign in to and are registered for.

settings.label: Client ID
settings.meaning: The application's OAuth client id: the audience of its access tokens. Usually the application id.

settings.label: Client secret
settings.meaning: Authenticates the backend for the code exchange and refresh at /oauth2/token.

settings.label: Tenant ID
settings.meaning: The tenant users are created in, when the API key isn't limited to one (sent as X-FusionAuth-TenantId).

settings.label: Issuer
settings.meaning: The iss every token must carry: the tenant's Issuer setting (acme.com unless changed, not the server URL).

settings.label: Webhook signing secret
settings.meaning: The HMAC key webhooks are signed with, when the webhook's signing key is an HMAC key. Without it, the signature is checked against the server's published keys.
settings.whereToFind: Settings › Webhooks › [your webhook] › Security › Signature: the signing key, from Settings › Key Master.

operations.name: users.login
operations.purpose: Signs a user in with their login id and password, or with a one-time password (after a password change). 212, 213 and 242 answer a pending sign-in.

operations.name: tokens.exchangeCode
operations.purpose: Exchanges the authorization code from FusionAuth's hosted login, with its PKCE verifier, for tokens.

operations.name: tokens.refresh
operations.purpose: Exchanges a refresh token for a new access token.

operations.name: tokens.revoke
operations.purpose: Revokes a refresh token (by the token, or by its id: the session).

operations.name: users.byEmail
operations.purpose: Reads the user with this email address.

operations.name: users.create
operations.purpose: Creates a user and registers them for the application.

operations.name: users.update
operations.purpose: Updates a user: here, sets their password.

operations.name: passwords.forgot
operations.purpose: Starts a password reset: FusionAuth emails the link, or returns its changePasswordId for the app to send.

operations.name: passwords.change
operations.purpose: Sets a new password with a changePasswordId.

operations.name: emailVerification.start
operations.purpose: Starts a new email verification without FusionAuth's email, for the app to send its code.

operations.name: emailVerification.verify
operations.purpose: Completes an email verification with its id and one-time code.

operations.name: passwordless.start
operations.purpose: Starts a passwordless sign-in and returns its code, for the app to send.

operations.name: passwordless.login
operations.purpose: Signs a user in with a passwordless code.

operations.name: jwks.get
operations.purpose: Reads the server's signing keys, for tokens and asymmetrically signed webhooks: when none are cached, when the cache expires, and when a token names a key not yet seen.

signature.description: The header is a JWT signed with the webhook's signing key (HS256/384/512 with the HMAC secret, or RSA/EC with a key from the server's JWKS). Verify it, refuse it when older than five minutes, and compare its request_body_sha256 claim with the base64 SHA-256 of the raw body.

events.meaning: A user was registered for an application.
Refresh tokens were revoked: a sign-out.
Users were added to a group.
Users were removed from a group.
